BURSEVI:v10p338/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p338/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p338/r2.claim: The two elevated paths are the ways of good and evil; the Prophet warns that the evil path must not be more beloved than the good one.
BURSEVI:v10p338/r2.anchor: هما النجدان نجد الخير ونجد الشر فلا يكن نجد لشر أحب إليكم من نجد الخير

BURSEVI:v10p338/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p338/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p338/r3.claim: Another reading takes the two paths as the two raised breasts, routes for milk that sustains and enables a newborn to nurse immediately after birth.
BURSEVI:v10p338/r3.anchor: أو طريقي الثديين لأنهما طريقان مرتفعان لنزول اللبن

BURSEVI:v10p338/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p338/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p338/r4.claim: Najd means elevated ground: good is ascent, while evil descends from innate nature into misery; evil may look elevated to the imaginative faculty, which explains figurative talk of rising toward things.
BURSEVI:v10p338/r4.anchor: وأصل النجد المكان المرتفع جعل الخير بمنزلة مكان مرتفع بخلاف الشر

BURSEVI:v10p338/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p338/r5.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p338/r5.claim: The paths are elevated because their clarity makes them as visible to reason as a high road is to the eye.
BURSEVI:v10p338/r5.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ لما وضحت الدلالة الدالة على الخير والشر صارتا كالطريقين المرتفعين

BURSEVI:v10p338/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p338/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p338/r6.claim: In the inward reading, the paths of spirit and heart are overcome respectively by the ego and by passion.
BURSEVI:v10p338/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى نجد الروح ونجد القلب فأبطلهما بغلبة النفس على الروح وغلبة الهوى على القلب

QASHANI:90:8-14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:90:8-14/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:90:8-14/r1.claim: Bodily faculties enable people to gain perfection, see lessons, ask about what they do not know, and speak; God directs them to good and evil paths.
QASHANI:90:8-14/r1.anchor: الآلات البدنية التي يتمكن بها من اكتساب الكمال ليبصر ما يعتبر به

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p324/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p324/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p324/r5.claim: God also guides people to the two moral paths, described in 76:3 and more explicitly in 91:7-10.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p324/r5.anchor: the Almighty has also guided him regarding the two paths

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p325/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p325/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p325/r1.claim: Human beings know good and evil; wrongdoing stems from being overcome by emotions despite that awareness, not from ignorance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p325/r1.anchor: knowing full well that he is committing evil

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p478/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p478/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p478/r3.claim: Najd is a high neck or path; the region Najd is named for rising above low-lying Tihama, and a verse by Imruʾ al-Qays illustrates the term.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p478/r3.anchor: النجد: العنق وجمعه نجود، وبه سميت نجد لارتفاعها عن انخفاض تهامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, and most authorities interpret the two high paths as the paths of good and evil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r8.anchor: قال ابن مسعود وابن عباس والجمهور: طريق الخير والشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي وابن المسيب والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r9.claim: Another view from Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAli, Ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Dahhak identifies the two paths as the two breasts that nourish a child.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p481/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا، وعلي وابن المسيب والضحاك: الثديين

MAJAZ:v2p299/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p299/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p299/r3.claim: Al-najdayn are two elevated paths, the path of good and the path of evil.
MAJAZ:v2p299/r3.anchor: «النجدين» (10) الطريقين فى ارتفاع، نجد الخير ونجد الشر

BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r1.claim: The two high paths are the routes of good and evil, or the two breasts; najd originally means elevated ground.
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r1.anchor: { وهدينه النجدين } طريقي الخير والشر، أو الثديين وأصله المكان المرتفع

NAHHAS:v5p229/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p229/r8.claim: For Basrans, the second object omits ilā; Sibawayh cites a poem as a parallel, while Kufans treat the word as an adverb like amāma or quddāma.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r8.anchor: مفعول ثان حذفت منه إلى على قول البصريين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r1.claim: The guidance imagery compares thought's effort to reach truth with travel on a road, and receiving Islam with a path difficult for the hearers; the passage also recalls God's provision of means for upright life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r1.anchor: ويتضمن ذلك تشبيه إعمال الفكر لنوال المطلوب بالسير في الطريق الموصل إلى المكان المرغوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r2.claim: Guidance may mean reason's direction to reflect on God's existence and oneness, explaining accountability for shirk without a messenger under one disputed theological position: Ashʿarites differ from Māturīdīs and Muʿtazilites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الهداية هداية العقل للتفكير في دلائل وجود الله ووحدانيته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484#2/r1.claim: Najd means an elevated path; al-Asmaʿi's verse uses anjud for high ground or mountain tracks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484#2/r1.anchor: والنجد: الطريق المرتفع، وأنشد الأصمعي: [الطويل] كميش الإزار خارج نصف ساقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r1.speaker: علي والحسن والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r1.claim: The two high paths are the clear ways of good and evil; najd denotes a conspicuous road rising above its surroundings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r1.anchor: سبيل الخير والشر قاله علي والحسن والفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they are the ways of guidance and misguidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r2.anchor: سبيل الهدى والضلال قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid interprets them as the paths to misery and happiness.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن المسيب، الضحاك، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the two high paths are the two breasts from which a child is nourished.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132#2/r4.anchor: الثديان ليتغذى بلبنهما روي عن ابن عباس أيضا وبه قال ابن المسيب والضحاك وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7415/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet promises safety from God's anger on the Resurrection Day to whoever recites Sūrat al-Balad.
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r1.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (البلد) أعطاه الله الأمن من غضبه

JISHUMI:v10p7415/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r2.claim: After al-Fajr's promise, warning, and account of the two groups, this chapter explains how success is attained and reinforces its oath.
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r2.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (الفجر) بالوعد والوعيد وذكر العبد وحال الفريقين، بين في هذه السورة ذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7415/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r10.claim: Al-najdayn are the two visible, elevated routes of good and evil; najd originally means high ground.
JISHUMI:v10p7415/r10.anchor: والنجدان: الطريقان، طريق الخير والشر، وأصل النجد: العلو

JISHUMI:v10p7416/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r9.claim: A fourth reading uses the body's wondrous capacities as evidence against the unbeliever and says God guided him, so his unbelief is his own doing.
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r9.anchor: وبدأ بالعين لعجيب خلقته في الرؤية، وباللسان لعجيب خلقته في الكلام

MUQATIL:90:5-16/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:90:5-16/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:90:5-16/r3.claim: God gave a person two eyes, a tongue, and two lips, and showed the two routes of good and evil.
MUQATIL:90:5-16/r3.anchor: { ألم نجعل له عينين ولسانا وشفتين وهديناه النجدين } [آية: 10] يقول: بينا له سبيل الخير

ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r10.claim: Al-najdayn are the two clear paths; najd is elevated ground, and the image means God made the paths of good and evil plain like two raised roads.
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r10.anchor: الطريقين الواضحين، النجد المرتفع من الأرض، فالمعنى ألم نعرفه طريق الخير وطريق الشر بينين

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r1.claim: The passage shifts from rhetorical questions to categorical judgment: a human endowed with insight and choice fails the moral standard, failing to take the steep path.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r1.anchor: Mit Beginn des dritten Gesätzes – das sich immer noch pronominal auf den in V. 90:4 eingeführten ʾinsān zurückbezieht – schlägt das zuvor von rhetorischen Fragen geprägte Register des Textes in einen kategorischen Tonfall um

TABATABAI:90:10-17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:10-17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:90:10-17/r1.claim: God taught the two paths by inspiration: people recognize good and distinguish it from evil, as in 91:7–8.
TABATABAI:90:10-17/r1.anchor: علمناه طريق الخير وطريق الشر بإلهام منا فهو يعرف الخير ويميزه من الشر

TABATABAI:90:1-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:1-20/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:90:1-20/r1.claim: When people said the two paths meant the mother's breasts, ʿAli answered that they mean good and evil.
TABATABAI:90:1-20/r1.anchor: قيل لأمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إن أناسا يقولون في قوله { وهديناه النجدين } أنهما الثديان

TABATABAI:90:1-20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:1-20/r2.speaker: الإمام الصادق
TABATABAI:90:1-20/r2.claim: Al-Kafi reports the Imam explaining the two heights as the paths of good and evil; similar reports are transmitted from ʿAli, Anas, Abu Umama, and others from the Prophet, and in al-Qummi.
TABATABAI:90:1-20/r2.anchor: عن حمزة بن محمد عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله تعالى { وهديناه النجدين } قال نجد الخير والشر

TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r1.speaker: علي
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r1.claim: The two elevated paths are the paths of good and evil; Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatada report the same.
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r1.anchor: أي سبيل الخير وسبيل الشر عن علي ع وابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r2.claim: An alternative interpretation is that God guided people to the two breasts; al-Dahhak and one Ibn ʿAbbas report transmit it.
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r2.anchor: معناه أرشدناه للثديين عن سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك

TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r3.speaker: علي
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r3.claim: Ali rejects the breasts interpretation and insists that the two paths are good and evil.
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس روي أنه قيل لأمير المؤمنين ع أن ناسا يقولون في قوله

TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r4.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r4.claim: A Prophetic report calls the ways the path of good and the path of evil, and asks why people would prefer evil.
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: بلغني أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r5.claim: Both ways are called elevated because they are visible to those morally responsible; avoiding evil can itself confer elevation and honor.
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r5.anchor: أن الطريقين جميعا ظاهران باديان للمكلفين فسمى سبحانه كلاهما نجدا لظهوره

TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r6.claim: Arab usage sometimes gives paired things one dual name, as al-qamaran means the sun and moon; al-Farazdaq supplies poetic evidence.
TABRISI:90:1-20#5/r6.anchor: إنه على عادة العرب في تثنية الأمرين إذا اتفقا على بعض الوجوه فيجري لفظ أحدهما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.claim: The surah's hardships call for patience: choosing either path, climbing the ascent, serving the enslaved, enduring famine, and caring for orphans and the destitute all demand perseverance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.anchor: وسلوك النجدين يحتاج إلى صبر لما في صعودهما وسلوكهما من تعب ونَصَب، واقتحام العقبة يحتاج إلى صبر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.claim: Patience comes first because the surah has already described human toil, the difficult ascent, and the two paths; mercy follows the subsequent duties of freeing and feeding.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.anchor: فقدم التواصي بالصبر لمّا تقدّم ما يدعو إليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r1.claim: The two paths may be the ways of good and evil or the two breasts, and both are gifts God guided people to.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r1.anchor: و"النجدان" يحتملان طريقي الخير والشر، ويحتملان الثديين وكلاهما هدانا ربنا إليهما

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says the two paths are the way of good and the way of evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه في قوله : وهديناه النجدين قال : سبيل الخير والشر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two paths are guidance and error.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وهديناه النجدين قال : الهدى والضلالة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r3.claim: The Prophet calls them two paths and asks why people choose the path of evil over the path of good.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r3.anchor: عن انس رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' هما نجدان ، فما جعل نجد الشر احب اليكم من نجد الخير

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r4.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas identifies the two heights as the two breasts.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#3/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : وهديناه النجدين قال : الثديين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r1.claim: The progression completes the foundations of learning: senses acquire knowledge, speech communicates it, and guidance helps distinguish and test good and evil.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r4.claim: Hidāyah is showing the route to a destination; najd is elevated terrain short of a mountain, and the two routes may be an ascent or a low hollow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r4.anchor: الدلالة على الطريق المبلغة إلى المكان المقصود السير إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r5.claim: Guidance is metaphorical for innate discernment of benefit and harm, grounding human society, knowledge and the Islamic path to salvation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r5.anchor: وقد استعيرت الهداية هنا للإلهام الذي جعله الله في الإنسان يدرك به الضار والنافع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r6.claim: The two high paths represent good and evil: good is hard to follow, while evil has hard consequences, explaining the next verse's image of an uphill pass.

TUSTARI:90:10/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:90:10/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:90:10/r1.claim: God showed humanity the paths of good to follow and evil to avoid; another interpretation is that the verse means governance.
TUSTARI:90:10/r1.anchor:
بينا له طريق الخير ليتبعه، وطريق الشر ليجتنبه، كما قال:
إنا هديناه السبيل

TUSTARI:90:10/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:90:10/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:90:10/r2.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the two heights to mean governance or administration.
TUSTARI:90:10/r2.anchor:
إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا
[الإنسان:3]. وقيل: يعني التدبير.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r14.claim: They interpret the two paths as the ways of good and evil that were shown to humanity, not as guidance meaning compulsion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r14.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود وابن عباس والناس: طريقا الخير والشر، أي عرضنا عليه طريقهما،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وعلي وابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وأبو وائل وأبو صالح ومحمد بن كعب والضحاك وعطاء الخراساني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.claim: They interpret the two roads as good and evil; Ibn Jarir later calls this the correct interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله -هو ابن مسعود-: {وهديناه النجدين} قال: الخير والشر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says there are two roads and asks why people prefer the road of evil to the good; the report is unique through Sinan ibn Saʿd, whom Ibn Maʿin trusted but Ahmad, al-Nasaʾi, and al-Juzajani called unreliable, and Ahmad abandoned his confused reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r2.anchor: عن سنان بن سعد، عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "هما نجدان، فما جعل نجد الشر أحب إليكم من نجد الخير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan transmits the Prophet's question about the two roads of good and evil as a mursal report; the same is sent without a Companion link by several transmitters and Qatada.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي رجاء قال: سمعت الحسن يقول: {وهديناه النجدين} قال: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the two high roads are the two breasts; similar reports come from al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym, Qatada, and Abu Hazim, but Ibn Jarir judges the good-and-evil interpretation correct.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وهديناه النجدين} قال: الثديين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r5.claim: The verse resembles the account of human creation and testing, where God grants hearing and sight and guides people to choose gratitude or disbelief.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404#2/r5.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية قوله: {إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج نبتليه فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا} [سورة الإنسان: 2، 3]

FARRA:v3p263/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p263/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p263/r12.claim: The two elevated paths are the paths of good and evil.
FARRA:v3p263/r12.anchor:
إنفاقه.
وقوله عز وجل: وهديناه النجدين (10) .
النجدان: سبيل الخير، وسبيل الشر.

FARRA:v3p263/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p263/r13.speaker: علي
FARRA:v3p263/r13.claim: ʿAlī is reported interpreting the two paths as good and evil.
FARRA:v3p263/r13.anchor: زياد بن علاقة عن أبي عمارة عن علي رحمه الله في قوله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#5/r1.claim: Najd is an elevated road; the two ways mean the paths of good and evil.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#5/r1.anchor:
{وهديناه النجدين} و"النجد": الطريق في ارتفاع. يريد: طريق الخير والشر.
وقال: ابن

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#5/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the two paths as the two breasts.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#5/r2.anchor:
النجدين} و"النجد": الطريق في ارتفاع. يريد: طريق الخير والشر.
وقال: ابن عباس

KASHSHAF:90:10/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:10/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:10/r1.claim: The two paths are the paths of good and evil.
KASHSHAF:90:10/r1.anchor: { وهديناه النجدين } أي : طريقي الخير والشر

KASHSHAF:90:10/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:10/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:90:10/r2.claim: Another view says the two high paths are the two breasts.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r2.claim: Al-najdayn means the paths of good and evil; another view takes them as the two breasts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r2.anchor: أي : طريقي الخير والشر . وقيل : الثديين

MAWARDI:90:10/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:10/r1.speaker: علي والحسن
MAWARDI:90:10/r1.claim: Ali and al-Hasan interpret the two elevated paths as the way of good and evil.
MAWARDI:90:10/r1.anchor: أحدها : سبيل الخير والشر ، قاله علي رضي الله عنه والحسن

MAWARDI:90:10/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:90:10/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets them as the way of guidance and misguidance.
MAWARDI:90:10/r2.anchor: الثاني : سبيل الهدى والضلالة ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:90:10/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:10/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:90:10/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets them as the paths of misery and happiness.
MAWARDI:90:10/r3.anchor: الثالث : سبيل الشقاء والسعادة ، قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI:90:10/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:10/r4.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن خثيم
MAWARDI:90:10/r4.claim: Qatada and al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym interpret them as the two breasts, provided for nourishment.
MAWARDI:90:10/r4.anchor: الرابع : الثديين ليتغذى بهما ، قاله قتادة والربيع بن خثيم

MAWARDI:90:10/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:10/r5.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI:90:10/r5.claim: Qutrub says najd is a raised road; Najd is elevated land while Tihama is low.
MAWARDI:90:10/r5.anchor: قال قطرب : والنجد هو الطريق المرتفع ، فأرض نجد هي المرتفعة ، وأرض تهامة هي المنخفضة

MAWARDI:90:10/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:10/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:10/r6.claim: By the same derivation, the two elevated routes could be Paradise and Hell.
MAWARDI:90:10/r6.anchor: ويحتمل على هذا الاشتقاق خامساً : أنهما الجنة والنار ، لارتفاعهما عن الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r18.speaker: علي والحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r18.claim: They identify the two paths as good and evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r18.anchor: سبيل الخير والشر , قاله علي رضي الله عنه والحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r19.claim: He identifies them as guidance and misguidance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r19.anchor: سبيل الهدى والضلالة , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r20.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r20.claim: He identifies them as misery and happiness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r21.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن خثيم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r21.claim: They identify the two peaks as the two breasts by which an infant is nourished.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r22.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r22.claim: He defines najd as a high road, distinguishing elevated Najd from low-lying Tihama.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r22.anchor: والنجد هو الطريق المرتفع , فأرض نجد هي المرتفعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r23.claim: Under the high-road derivation, the two peaks could be Paradise and Fire because they rise above the earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r23.anchor: أنهما الجنة والنار , لارتفاعهما عن الأرض

MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two paths are the way of good and the way of evil, which God made known to humanity.
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ﴿ وهديناه النجدين ﴾ قال هديناه السبيلين سبيل الخير وسبيل الشر

MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r2.claim: Ibn Masud likewise says God guided humanity to the path of good and the path of evil.
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال يقول ﴿ هديناه ﴾ سبيل الخير وسبيل الشر

MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r3.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib gives the same explanation: the two paths are good and evil.
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r3.anchor: عن أبي عمارة عن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام مثله

MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r4.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r4.claim: Mujahid gives the same explanation: the two paths are good and evil.

MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r5.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MUJAHID:v2p759#3/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak gives the same explanation: the two paths are good and evil.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#8/r1.claim: The two paths are the ways of good and evil leading to Paradise and Hell; another view takes them as the two breasts.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#8/r1.anchor: طريقى الخير والشر المفضيين إلى الجنة والنار وقيل الثديين

QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r1.claim: The two najds are the elevated roads of good and evil, shown to humanity through the messengers.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r1.anchor: والنجد. الطريق في ارتفاع. وهذا قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r2.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet’s teaching that the two routes are good and evil, and people are not made to prefer evil.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r2.anchor:
وروى قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول:
" يا أيها الناس، إنما هما النجدان: نجد الخير، ونجد الشر

QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r3.speaker: عكرمة، سعيد بن المسيب، الضحاك، ابن عباس، علي
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r3.claim: They interpret the two najds as the two breasts, pathways to an infant’s life and nourishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r3.anchor: وروي عن عكرمة قال: النجدان: الثديان. وهو قول سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك، وروي عن ابن عباس وعلي

QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r4.claim: Najd means an elevated road; its plural is nujud, and the region Najd is named for rising above low Tihama.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r4.anchor: فالنجد: العلو، وجمعه نجود ومنه سميت «نجد»

QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:90:10/r5.claim: Imru al-Qays’s line attests the word Najd as an elevated route.

QUTB-ZILAL:90:10/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:10/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:10/r1.claim: People are equipped to recognize good and evil, guidance and error, and can direct themselves along either path; this dual capacity serves God's wise purpose in creation.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:10/r1.anchor: ففي طبيعته هذا الاستعداد المزدوج لسلوك أي النجدين

QUTB-ZILAL:90:10/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:10/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:10/r2.claim: This verse reveals human nature and, with the passage in Surat al-Shams, forms a basis for the Islamic account of the psyche.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:10/r2.anchor: هي والآيات الأخرى في سورة الشمس

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r3.claim: The segment gives only the verse text about eyes, tongue, lips, and the two paths, without commentary on those verses.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r3.anchor: ألم نجعل له عينين * ولسانا وشفتين * وهديناه النجدين

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r1.claim: The created eyes, tongue, lips, and guidance to two paths demonstrate God's power against the disbeliever's claim that no one can overpower him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r1.anchor: ألم نجعل له عينين * ولسانا وشفتين * وهديناه النجدين

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r2.claim: Najd means an elevated road; clear proofs resemble it because they are evident to minds as a high road is to sight.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r2.anchor: قال أهل العربية : النجد الطريق في ارتفاع

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r3.speaker: عامة المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r3.claim: Most exegetes understand the two paths as the paths of good and evil.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r3.anchor: وإلى هذا التأويل ذهب عامة المفسرين في النجدين

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying the two paths are good and evil, and one should not prefer evil's path to good's.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r4.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة أنه عليه السلام قال : إنما هما النجدان

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r5.claim: This guidance recalls the passage saying humanity was guided to a path and may be grateful or ungrateful.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية كالآية في : { هل أتى على الإنسان }

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib identify the two paths as the breasts, routes to an infant's life and provision; God guides the infant to suckle.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r7.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب ، أنهما الثديان

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r8.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r8.claim: Al-Qaffal prefers the good-and-evil interpretation and argues that the creator of a rational heart and articulate tongue can destroy what He made and knows what creatures conceal.

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r9.claim: Manifest gifts leave no excuse for disbelief or for using God-given wealth to taunt God and the supporters of His religion.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r9.anchor: فما العذر في الذهاب عن هذا مع وضوحه

STUDYQURAN:90:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:10/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:90:10/r1.claim: The two highways mean good and evil; a hadith urges people not to prefer the evil path, and commentators link the verse to God's guidance in 76:3.
STUDYQURAN:90:10/r1.anchor: The two highways are interpreted to be those of good and evil

STUDYQURAN:90:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:10/r2.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:90:10/r2.claim: A hadith warns that there are only two paths, good and evil, and people should not make evil more beloved.
STUDYQURAN:90:10/r2.anchor: O people! There are only two highways: the highway of good and the highway of evil

SAMIN-DURR:90:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:10/r1.claim: Al-najdayn may be a locative, or require an omitted preposition if it means the two breasts.
SAMIN-DURR:90:10/r1.anchor: إما ظرف، وإما على حذف الجار إن أريد بهما الثديان،

SAMIN-DURR:90:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:10/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:10/r2.claim: Najd originally means the raised neck, or an elevated road; Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses najd for the high Najd of Kabkab, as the region is elevated above Tihāma.
SAMIN-DURR:90:10/r2.anchor: وقيل: الطريق العالي، كقول امرئ القيس:

TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd interprets the two paths as good and evil.
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله، {وهديناه النجدين} [البلد: 10] قال: الخير والشر

TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains them as guidance and error, or the paths of good and evil.
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r2.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وهديناه النجدين} [البلد: 10] يقول: الهدى والضلالة

TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says the two paths are good and evil.
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {وهديناه النجدين} [البلد: 10] قال: الخير والشر

TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid calls them the paths of good and evil.

TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r5.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r5.claim: Al-Rabīʿ b. Khuthaym rejects the interpretation that the two paths are the breasts.
TAB-FULL:v24p415#2/r5.anchor: عن الربيع بن خثيم، قال: «ليسا بالثديين»

TAB-FULL:v24p418/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the two paths as good and evil.
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r1.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {وهديناه النجدين} [البلد: 10] : نجد الخير، ونجد الشر

TAB-FULL:v24p418/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r2.claim: A report through al-Ḥasan attributes to the Prophet the teaching that the two paths are good and evil and asks why people prefer evil.
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " هما نجدان: نجد خير، ونجد شر، فما جعل نجد الشر أحب إليكم من نجد الخير

TAB-FULL:v24p418/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r3.claim: Qatāda reports the same prophetic teaching about the two paths of good and evil.
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {وهديناه النجدين} [البلد: 10] ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: «أيها الناس، إنما هما النجدان

TAB-FULL:v24p418/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd describes the person as shown the road of both good and evil, linking it to God's guidance of the path.
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله: {وهديناه النجدين} [البلد: 10] : قاطع طريق الخير والشر

TAB-FULL:v24p418/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r5.claim: Others interpret the two paths as the two breasts, the routes by which an infant receives milk.
TAB-FULL:v24p418/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: وهديناه الثديين: سبيلي اللبن الذي يتغذى به

TAB-FULL:v24p419/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p419/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p419/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk are reported to interpret the two paths as the two breasts.
TAB-FULL:v24p419/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وهديناه النجدين} [البلد: 10] قال: هما الثديان

TAB-FULL:v24p419/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p419/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p419/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the paths of good and evil: although the breasts are routes for milk, the context counts divine guidance to the good path as a blessing, as in Sūrat al-Insān.
TAB-FULL:v24p419/r2.anchor: وأولى القولين بالصواب في ذلك عندنا: قول من قال: عني بذلك طريق الخير والشر

THALABI:v10p209/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p209/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v10p209/r2.claim: Most commentators say God showed people the elevated paths of good and evil, truth and falsehood, guidance and error, as in 76:3.
THALABI:v10p209/r2.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين: يعني بينا له طريق الخير والشر والحق والباطل والهدى والضلالة

THALABI:v10p209/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p209/r3.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v10p209/r3.claim: A report from al-Ḥasan attributes to the Prophet the statement that the two elevated paths are the path of good and the path of evil, asking why people prefer the latter.
THALABI:v10p209/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه: «إنما هما نجدان نجد الخير ونجد الشر

THALABI:v10p209/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p209/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p209/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk instead say the two paths are the two breasts; najd means a road on high ground, as a poetic line illustrates.
THALABI:v10p209/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب عن ابن عباس في قوله سبحانه: وهديناه النجدين قال: الثديين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r1.claim: “Najd” is elevated ground or a high road; it refers to land rising above the lowlands of Tihama.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r1.anchor: النجد: معناه في اللغة: ما ارتفع من الأرض، وأشرف، ونجد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، عبد الله، علي، مجاهد، مقاتل، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r2.claim: The two highroads are the paths of good and evil, obedience and disobedience, as in 76:3.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r2.anchor: يريد بينا له طريق الخير، وطريق الشر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r3.claim: God made the ways of good and evil clear to a person like two visibly raised roads.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r3.anchor: المعنى: ألم نعرفه طريق الخير والشر بينين كتبيين الطريقين العاليين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن المسيب، الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r4.claim: An alternative identifies the two highroads as the two breasts; the author rejects it as unlikely, though its proponents compare them to paths for an infant’s nourishment and say God guides the infant to suckle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p22/r4.anchor: وروى عيسى بن عقال (5)، عن أبيه (6) عن ابن عباس في

WAHIDI-QT:90:10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:90:10/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:90:10/r1.claim: God made known the two paths: good and evil.
WAHIDI-QT:90:10/r1.anchor: { وهديناه النجدين } يقول ألم نعرفه طريق الخير وطريق الشر

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r6.claim: Najd literally means a raised tract or mound; Arabia's elevated region includes Hijaz Najd and Arid Najd, and another place called Najd lies near Mahra in Yemen.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r7.claim: By extension, najd evokes a high open road, elevated rank or difficult achievement, a courageous person, grief, overcoming an opponent, sweating, or bravery.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r7.anchor: Yüksek ve açık yola, âlî mertebelere çıkan, yüksek işler gören adama

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r8.claim: Najd can also mean the breast or udder because of its swelling; Arabs swore by a mother's breasts, as in a Turkish oath invoking the milk one suckled.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r8.anchor: “inan ana memelerine kasem olsun ki yapmadım” diye yemin etmek şâyi‘dir

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r9.claim: Although the word evokes its other senses, context with hardship and the coming steep ascent favors two elevated goals or paths for a striving champion.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r9.anchor: iki tepe gibi yüksek iki gaye, iki yol mânası telkin etmektedir.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك، علي
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r10.claim: Some infer two breasts from the sequence of bodily gifts; the source says this interpretation is transmitted from Ibn Abbas, Dahhak, and Ali.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r10.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan ve Dahhâk’ten ve hatta Hazret-i Ali’den rivayet edenler de olmuştur.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r11.claim: Though nursing is a divine mercy, it is a general early-life provision rather than the distinctive human gift or future moral duty indicated by the passage.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r11.anchor: insan dilinin ve dudağının temayüz ettiği nimetlerden olmadığı gibi

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r12.claim: The stronger transmitted and reasoned interpretation is that the two elevated routes lead to good and evil, as in the verse about showing the way and leaving a person grateful or ungrateful.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r12.anchor: biri hayr biri şer iki yüksek gayeye giden, biri meymenetli biri meş’um iki yüksek tarîk mânasına olduğunu daha sahih ve daha kuvvetli rivayet ve dirayetle teyid

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r13.claim: Bukhari transmits Mujahid's interpretation as good and evil.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r13.anchor: Buhârî de Mücâhid’den hayr u şer demiştir.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r14.speaker: ربيع بن خثيم
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r14.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits Rabi ibn Khuthaym as denying that the two routes mean two breasts.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r15.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r15.claim: Ibn Masud glosses the two routes as guidance and misguidance, the paths of good and evil.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r15.anchor: Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd’dan: وَهَدَيْنَٰهُ ٱلنَّجْدَيْنِ Hüdâ ve dalâlet, sebîlü’l-hayri ve’ş-şer.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r16.speaker: عكرمة، مجاهد، الضحاك
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r16.claim: Ikrima, Mujahid, and Dahhak also explain the two routes as good and evil.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r16.anchor: İkrime’den ve Mücâhid’den: Hayr u şer.[^11] Dahhâk’ten: Necdü’l-hayri ve necdü’ş-şer.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r17.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r17.claim: Hasan's mursal and Qatada's report from the Prophet call them the good and evil routes and say evil was not made more beloved than good.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r17.anchor: Onlar iki necddir: Necd-i hayr ve necd-i şer, demek ki necd-i şer, size necd-i hayrdan daha sevgili kılınmamıştır.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r18.speaker: ابن زيد
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r18.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses them as the good and evil paths and cites God's statement that He showed the way.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r18.anchor: İbn Zeyd’den: Ve hedeynâhü’n-necdeyn’de “tarîk-i hayr ve şer” dedi

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r19.speaker: الحاكم، الطبراني
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r19.claim: Al-Hakim calls Ibn Masud's report sound; Tabarani and others transmit it, and Tabarani also reports a Prophetic version from Abu Umama.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r19.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan Hâkim sahih[^13] demiş[^14], Taberânî ve daha başkaları da rivayet eylemiş

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r20.speaker: علي
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r20.claim: Durr al-Manthur reports through Firyabi and Abd ibn Humayd that Ali rejected the breast interpretation and said the routes mean good and evil; Alusi notes the report in Majma al-Bayan too.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r20.anchor: Hazret-i Ali kerremallahu vechehu “bazı insanlar ‘necdeyn sedyeyn’ diyorlar, hayır onlar hayr u şerdir”

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r21.claim: The Prophetic wording rejects the claim that human nature loves evil more than good: human nature is equally receptive to both, and dominance comes from secondary causes.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r21.anchor: Bununla birtakımlarının zannettiği gibi insan fıtratının hayırdan ziyade şerri sevdiği ve binâen‘aleyh insanda şer meylinin asıl olduğu davası reddedilmiş demektir.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r22.claim: As discussed in al-Baqara, Adam's lapse came from Satan's seduction; an evil-commanding soul follows ignorance or corruption through bad upbringing and habit, not an evil human essence.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r23.claim: Human injustice or moral progress is not universally fixed by nature; secondary causes shape character, which can be refined or corrupted through training.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r23.anchor: göre ahlâkını tehzib veya ifsad edebilir.

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r1.claim: The poet who treats injustice as innate and virtue as an accidental defect is wrong; people can develop either capacity through secondary causes.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r1.anchor: nüfûsta zulmü hılkī ve tabîî addedip de

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r2.claim: The evil route is actually a low abyss, but travelers imagine it as elevation like good; usage calls both routes najd by predominance because good is the true height.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r2.anchor: gālib olduğu için tağlib tarîkiyle ikisine de “necd” ıtlak edilmiş

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r3.claim: A person's natural love of benefits received and dislike of harm received differs from the moral ideal of loving good for itself and rejecting evil for itself, especially when acts affect others.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r3.anchor: insanın kendisine başkasından gelen hayr u şerre nisbeti ile

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r4.claim: Because material nature prefers rest, a weak and lazy person wants benefits without effort and avoids both good and evil action; evil can be as difficult as good.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r4.anchor: Firavun olmak Firavun ile uğraşmaktan kolay değildir.

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r5.claim: Both active paths stand like peaks against inertia and require courage; people do not inherently prefer evil, and whichever disposition develops determines their end.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r5.anchor: Zikrolunan hadis gösteriyor ki insan fıtratında hayr devâ‘îsi, şer devâ‘îsinden az değildir.

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r6.claim: From helpless infancy people are surrounded by good and evil, pleasure and pain; hardship means God protects and raises them until they can act.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r6.anchor: O ne kendine ne başkasına bir hayr yapmaya ne de kendisinden şerri def‘etmeye bizzat kādir olmadığı hâlde Allah teâlâ onu o meşakkat âlemi içinde dilediği kadar korur

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r7.claim: Once capable, a person must thank God by choosing good and avoiding harm to self and God's servants according to their ability.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r7.anchor: istitâ‘ati nisbetinde O’nun şükrünü îfâ için hayrı şerri temyiz ederek hayr yapmak, kendine ve ibâdullâha şerden sakınmak ile mükelleftir

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r8.claim: Both goals demand movement, patience, and endurance: one leads upward to safety, the other downward to ruin, so both are like peaks to cross.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r8.anchor: birinde i‘tilâ ve selâmet, birinde de sukūt ve felâket muhakkak olan iki tepe gibidir

ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r9.claim: Guidance to both peaks means pointing to both routes: encourage good as commanding right and warn against evil as forbidding wrong; good is positive and evil negative.
ELMALILI:90:8-10#2/r9.anchor: hayrı emir emr bi’lma‘rûf, şerden nehy nehy ani’l-münker demektir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r12.claim: This passage explains the two routes in al-Balad: fujur and taqwa; guidance makes their natures clear, forbidding the former and commanding the latter.

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r1.claim: Naǧd literally means highland opposite lowland, but can also mean an elevated, clearly visible path, a sense supported by a likely authentic Imruʾ al-Qais line.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Naǧd ist eigentlich „Hochland“ im Gegensatz zu ġaur, „Bodensenke“

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r2.claim: The use of hadā with al-sabīl in 76:3 supports understanding naǧd here as a path; exegetes take the two paths as good and evil, which fits the binary dual and the comparison with 91:8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Überdies heißt es in 76:3: ʾinnā hadaināhu s-sabīla – zweites Objekt des auch im vorliegenden Vers gebrauchten Verbs hadā ist also as-sabīl, „der Weg“

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r3.claim: The height connotation likely recedes behind clear visibility, making naǧd a general clear path, broader than ʿaqaba in the next verse.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Die Konnotation der Höhe tritt aber wohl hinter diejenige der deutlichen Erkennbarkeit zurück, so dass naǧd einfach nur „klarer Weg“ bedeutet

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r4.speaker: Ahrens
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r4.claim: Ahrens instead explains the dual as imposed by rhyme, with naǧdayn referring only to the virtuous path; the author finds the literal good-and-evil dual more convincing.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:10:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Alternativ könnte man den Dual mit Ahrens lediglich auf Reimzwang zurückführen

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza resumes the human-being statement at the introduction’s end and consists of two triplets marked by rhyme; the repeated third-person polemical questions formally unify them.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz, das pronominal an den ʾinsān-Spruch am Ende des Einleitungsgesätzes anknüpft, gliedert sich in zwei reimlich voneinander abgesetzte Dreiergruppen

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r5.claim: The second triplet lists God’s gifts of sight, speech, and moral direction, recalling the human being’s creation in 90:4; its rhyme shift accents the contrast with human self-importance.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r5.anchor: Gottes Ausstattung des Menschen mit Sehsinn, Sprechwerkzeugen und moralischer Orientierung aufzählt und damit auf die bereits in V. 90:4 festgehaltene Geschaffenheit des Menschen zurückverweist

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r6.claim: The two paths mean reverence for God and vice, as specified in 91:8; the repeated dual endings tie divine gifts and human duty to the moral opposition between good and evil.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r6.anchor: dass es sich um die dem Menschen aufgegebene Entscheidung zwischen „zwei Wegen“, an-naǧdain, also zwischen „Gottesfurcht“ und „Laster“ (91:8) handelt

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r1.claim: Continuing al-Tibyan’s proof, the author argues that God who taught people the two paths is even more deserving of knowledge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r1.anchor: ومن جعله عالماً بنجدي الخير والشر - وهما طريقاهما - أليس هو أولى وأحق بالعلم منه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r4.speaker: لسان العرب
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r4.claim: Najd means high, firm, elevated ground, like a hard ridge rising before a traveler.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r4.anchor: جاء في (لسان العرب) : "النجد من الأرض قفافها وصلابها، وما غلظ منها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r5.claim: The two elevated paths are most commonly understood as good and evil; another view identifies them as the two breasts.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r5.anchor: والمقصود بالنجدين: طريقا الخير والشر. وقيل: الثديان. والأول أشهر وهو الذي ذهب إليه عامة المفسرين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r6.speaker: الرسول
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s explanation that the two paths are those of good and evil, and that one should not prefer the evil path.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r6.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة أنه عليه السلام قال: "إنما هما النجدان، نَجْدُ الخير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p264/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p264/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p264/r1.claim: The surah uses najd rather than other Quranic terms for a path because climbing a height is difficult, matching human toil and the hard obstacle.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p264/r1.anchor: ذلك أن التعبير مناسب لجو السورة فإن سُلوكَ النجدِ فيه مشقةٌ وصعوبة لما فيه من صعود وارتفاع

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports the Prophet's rhetorical question: the two high roads are good and evil, so why prefer the road of evil?
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ وهديناه النجدين ﴾ قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the two high roads as the two breasts.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي أن ابن عباس قال في قوله تعالى ﴿ وهديناه النجدين ﴾ قال الثديين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd interprets them as the path of good and the path of evil.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p374/r3.anchor: عن زر بن حبيش عن ابن مسعود قال في قوله تعالى ﴿ وهديناه النجدين ﴾ قال سبيل الخير وسبيل الشر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r1.claim: The established interpretation is the two ways of good and evil, reported from Ibn Masʿud with al-Hakim's authentication, from Ibn Abbas, and from ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak, and others; Abu Umama transmits it from the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r1.anchor: أي طريقي الخير والشر كما أخرجه الحاكم وصححه والطبراني وغيرهما عن ابن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r2.claim: Najd is a raised road; al-Alusi cites a line by Imruʾ al-Qays about crossing Najd and explains the region's height relative to Tihama.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r2.anchor: والنجد مشهور في الطريق المرتفع قال امرؤ القيس فريقان منهم جازع بطن نخلة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r3.claim: The blessing lies in making clear which route saves and which ruins; the blessing does not depend on the person choosing the good route.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r3.anchor: والأمتنان المحدث عنه بأن هداه سبحانه وبين له تعالى شأنه ما أن سلكه نجا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r4.claim: Al-Imam links this to 76:3: God showed the human the way, whether grateful or ungrateful.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r4.anchor: وقد جعل الإمام هذه الآية كقوله تعالى إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r5.claim: Calling the good path elevated is apt; evil is a descent from innate human nature to misery, either by contrast or by imagining the climb toward it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r5.anchor: ووصف سبيل الخير بالرفعة والنجدة ظاهر بخلاف سبيل الشرفان فيه هبوطا من ذروة الفطرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r6.claim: An alternative from Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Musayyib identifies the two heights as the mother's breasts: paired routes providing an infant life and nourishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم من طرق عن ابن عباس أنهما الثديان روي ذلك عن ابن المسيب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r7.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r7.claim: A report says Ali rebuked people who claimed the heights meant breasts and clarified that they are good and evil; al-Alusi allows that the alternative relies on the wording and obvious benefaction.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#5/r7.anchor: ونسب هذا التفسير لعلي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أيضا والمذكور في الدر المنثور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r5.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r5.claim: Most commentators say the two high paths are good and evil, truth and falsehood, or guidance and error, as in the verse that calls people either grateful or ungrateful.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r5.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين: طريق الخير والشر، والحق والباطل، والهدى والضلالة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r6.claim: Muhammad b. Kaʿb reports Ibn Abbas’s interpretation of the two paths as the two breasts; saʿid b. al-Musayyab and al-Dahhak share it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب عن ابن عباس: "وهديناه النجدين" قال: الثديين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r7.claim: Najd is a road rising to a height.

BINTSHATI:v1p181/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r2.claim: Hudā originally evokes a protruding stone that keeps a traveler from stumbling, daylight that reveals the road, then a caravan’s leading camel and guide; it came to mean guidance rather than error and, religiously, inspiration or enabling grace.
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r2.anchor: في الهداية ضد الضلال، وهو أكثر المعاني

BINTSHATI:v1p181/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r3.claim: Najd means elevated ground or a clear uphill road; related forms describe tall, forward-moving camels and came to suggest a visible guide leading a people.
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r3.anchor: والنجد لغة: ما أشرف من الأرض، والطريق المرافع الواضح

BINTSHATI:v1p181/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r4.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib interprets the two paths as truth and falsehood in belief, truth and lies in speech, and good and bad in action.
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r4.anchor: وفسر "الراغب" النجدين في الآية، بطريق الحق والباطل

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r1.speaker: الجمهور
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r1.claim: The majority, including al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn al-Qayyim, and Muḥammad ʿAbduh, take the two heights as the paths of good and evil.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r1.anchor: وذكر "أبو حيان" أن هذا هو ما عليه الجمهور

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r2.claim: A view in al-Asās, al-Baḥr, and al-Muḥīṭ identifies the two paths as breasts nourishing a child; the author considers this strained and weak.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r2.anchor: والتأويل به، فيه شطط التكلف مع ظهور وهنه وضعفه

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r3.claim: ‘We guided him’ implies God inspired innate human discrimination of good and evil and supplied sensory means; the unique Qur’anic word najdayn highlights the paths’ visible clarity.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r3.anchor: الهدى ملحوظ فيه أنه تعالى ألهم الفطرة الإنسانية الإدراك المميز للخير والشر

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r4.claim: The sequence shows a human equipped with senses and innate discernment to bear the difficult trust of moral responsibility and choose between the clearly visible paths.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r4.anchor: فهذا الإنسان الذي خلقه الله مهيأ لأمانة التكليف الصعبة

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r6.claim: The past and future references show that God governs the human being’s entire course, from creation to final return; the discussion invokes the opening revelation’s warning about human arrogance.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r6.anchor: بيان لمدى إحاطة الله بالإنسان مهما يبلغ من قوته وطغيانه

BINTSHATI:v1p183/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p183/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p183/r1.claim: God owns human destiny across past and future: He is the creator, and to Him is the return, as stated in the first revealed sūra.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r7.claim: The past-tense guidance describes reason as a fixed, innate faculty, unlike the continually renewed bodily instruments; reason makes a person accountable.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r7.anchor: اختير له لفظ الماضي لذلك تحقيقا لكونه وجعله غريزة لا تتحول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r8.claim: The two elevated paths are good and evil; through reason humans know both and become responsible.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r8.anchor: وصار بما جعلناه له من ذلك سميعا بصيرا عالما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r9.claim: The Prophet says there are two roads, good and evil, and that what is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and distracting; al-Mundhirī glosses najd as a road.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r9.anchor: إنما هما نجدان : نجد خير ونجد شر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r10.claim: Good and evil are called elevated roads because each raises humans above animals and requires effort; divine aid can make either path easy or difficult.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r10.anchor: عبر عن الخير والشر به لإعلائهما الإنسان عن رتبة باقي الحيوان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r11.claim: The sound primordial nature recognizes and rejects evil and recognizes and urges good, although desires contend with it; prophetic sayings describe this moral recognition.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r11.anchor: البر ما اطمأنت إليه النفس وانشرح له الصدر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r12.claim: People have acquired capacity rather than autonomous independence; God creates their acts while making them answerable through revealed guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r12.anchor: بل كان هذا المنكر عليه لم يؤهل لطريق الخير

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r11.speaker: ناس
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r11.claim: Some people say the two paths mean the two breasts; Ali's response continues in the next segment.
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r11.anchor: إن ناسا يقولون: إن النجدين الثديين

DURR-FULL:v8p522/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r1.claim: Ali answers that the two paths are the paths of good and evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r1.anchor: قال: الخير والشر وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن عكرمة والضحاك رضي الله عنهما مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p522/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r2.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r2.claim: They agree that the two paths are good and evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة والضحاك رضي الله عنهما مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p522/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r3.claim: A report through Anas says the two paths are good and evil and asks why anyone would prefer the evil path.
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r3.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: هما نجدان فما جعل نجد الشر أحب إليكم من نجد الخير

DURR-FULL:v8p522/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r4.claim: Al-Hasan transmits the Prophet's warning not to prefer the path of evil over the path of good.
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {وهديناه النجدين} قال: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول

DURR-FULL:v8p522/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r5.claim: The Prophet tells people that the two paths are good and evil and warns against preferring evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r5.anchor: عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يا أيها الناس إنما هما نجدان نجد خير ونجد شر

DURR-FULL:v8p522/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r6.claim: Qatada relays the same Prophetic description of good and evil as two paths.
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: فذكر مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p522/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r7.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says the two paths are good and evil and urges that evil not be preferred.
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إنما هما نجدان نجد الخير ونجد الشر

DURR-FULL:v8p522/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r8.claim: A separate interpretation identifies the two paths as the two breasts.
DURR-FULL:v8p522/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {وهديناه النجدين} قال: الثديين

NASHR:v1p203/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p203/r1.claim: Later authorities wrongly limited qalqala to stopping because they took earlier scholars’ use of waqf to mean pause, though it meant consonant sukun.
NASHR:v1p203/r1.anchor: تخصيص القلقلة بالوقف تمسكا بظاهر ما رأوه من عبارة المتقدمين

NASHR:v1p203/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p203/r2.claim: Qalqala is not a vowel or movement; it becomes more perceptible at an actual pause, which likely reinforced the mistaken restriction.
NASHR:v1p203/r2.anchor: كون القلقلة في الوقف العرفي أبين وحسبانهم أن القلقلة حركة وليس كذلك

NASHR:v1p203/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r3.speaker: الخليل
NASHR:v1p203/r3.claim: Al-Khalīl defines qalqala as forceful calling out and laqlaqa as forceful sound.
NASHR:v1p203/r3.anchor: فقد قال الخليل: القلقلة شدة الصياح، واللقلقة شدة الصوت.

NASHR:v1p203/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p203/r4.claim: Citing Shurayḥ and al-Mubarrad, Ibn al-Jazarī says the jīm in النجدين is a medial qalqala and that it is clearer at pause on final than on medial letters.
NASHR:v1p203/r4.anchor: فالقلقلة هنا أبين في الوقف في المتطرفة من المتوسطة

NASHR:v1p203/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r5.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v1p203/r5.claim: Most authorities consider alif the strongest madd letter; Ibn al-Faḥḥām instead ranks wāw, then yāʾ, then alif.
NASHR:v1p203/r5.anchor: وأمكنهن عند الجمهور الألف وأبعد ابن الفحام فقال: أمكنهن في المد الواو،

NASHR:v1p203/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r6.speaker: ابن الفحام
NASHR:v1p203/r6.claim: Ibn al-Faḥḥām ranks wāw strongest for madd, followed by yāʾ and then alif.
NASHR:v1p203/r6.anchor: وأبعد ابن الفحام فقال: أمكنهن في المد الواو، ثم الياء، ثم الألف،

NASHR:v1p203/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r7.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v1p203/r7.claim: The majority derive fatḥa from alif, ḍamma from wāw, and kasra from yāʾ.
NASHR:v1p203/r7.anchor: والجمهور على أن الفتحة من الألف والضمة من الواو والكسرة من الياء.

NASHR:v1p203/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p203/r8.claim: Authorities differ on whether letters precede vowels, vowels precede letters, or neither derives from the other; some authorities judge the third account correct.
NASHR:v1p203/r8.anchor: وقيل: عكس ذلك، وقيل: ليست الحركات مأخوذة من الحروف ولا الحروف مأخوذة من الحركات وصححه بعضهم.

NASHR:v1p203/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p203/r9.claim: The four hidden letters are hāʾ and the three madd letters; they hide in connected speech, while hāʾ is strengthened by ṣila and madd letters by lengthening before hamza.
NASHR:v1p203/r9.anchor: والحروف الخفية أربعة الهاء وحروف المد سميت خفية لأنها تخفى في اللفظ

NASHR:v1p203/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p203/r10.claim: The two līn letters are wāw and yāʾ when sākin and preceded by fatḥ.
NASHR:v1p203/r10.anchor: وحرفا اللين الواو والياء الساكنتان المفتوح ما قبلهما.

NASHR:v1p203/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p203/r11.claim: The correct view makes lām and rāʾ the two letters of inḥirāf; another view, attributed to Basrans, counts only lām, because these letters turn from their articulation points.
NASHR:v1p203/r11.anchor: وحرفا الانحراف اللام والراء على الصحيح، وقيل: اللام فقط، ونسب إلى البصريين،

NASHR:v1p203/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p203/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p203/r12.claim: Nūn and mīm are the two ghunna letters, also called al-aghannān because their nasalization is connected to the nasal cavity.
NASHR:v1p203/r12.anchor: وحرفا الغنة هما النون والميم، ويقال لهما الأغنان لما فيهما من الغنة المتصلة بالخيشوم.

ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r1.claim: Najd means a neck, with plural nujūd.

ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r2.claim: Najd means a high road; the region takes its name from elevation above low-lying Tihāmah.
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r2.anchor: وبه سميت نجد لارتفاعها عن انخفاض تهامة ،   والنجد : الطريق العالي

ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r3.speaker: امرؤ القيس
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r3.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's verse is cited as poetic evidence for the term's usage.
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r3.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس : فريقان منهم جازع بطن نخله

ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and most commentators understand the two roads as the paths of good and evil.
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r4.anchor: قال ابن مسعود وابن عباس والجمهور : طريق الخير والشر

ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي وابن المسيب والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also, with ʿAlī, Ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, interprets them as the two breasts, routes for the child's life and nourishment.
ABUHAYYAN:90:10/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضاً ،   وعليّ وابن المسيب والضحاك : الثديين

ALUSI:90:10/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:10/r1.claim: The two elevated paths are the way of good and the way of evil; God makes clear which path brings salvation and which brings ruin.

ALUSI:90:10/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
ALUSI:90:10/r2.claim: Al-Ḥākim authenticated Ibn Masʿūd’s report of the good-and-evil interpretation; it is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others.
ALUSI:90:10/r2.anchor: كما أخرجه الحاكم وصححه والطبراني وغيرهما عن ابن مسعود وأخرجه عبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن ابن عباس

ALUSI:90:10/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI:90:10/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī also transmits this interpretation from Abū Umāma as a report traced to the Prophet.
ALUSI:90:10/r3.anchor: وأخرجه الطبراني عن أبي أمامة مرفوعاً

ALUSI:90:10/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:10/r4.claim: In ordinary usage, najd is an elevated road; Imruʾ al-Qays’s line uses Najd Kabkab for a highland route.
ALUSI:90:10/r4.anchor: والنجد مشهور في الطريق المرتفع قال امرؤ القيس

ALUSI:90:10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:10/r5.claim: The region Najd takes its name from its height above low-lying Tihāma.
ALUSI:90:10/r5.anchor: وسميت نجد به لارتفاعها عن انخفاض تهامة

ALUSI:90:10/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:10/r6.claim: The blessing lies in showing the person the paths, so that one leads to salvation and the other to ruin; the favor does not depend on actually choosing good.
ALUSI:90:10/r6.anchor: والامتنان المحدث عنه بأن هداه سبحانه وبين له تعالى شأنه ما إن سلكه نجا وما أن سلكه هلك ولا يتوقف الامتنان على سلوك طريق الخير

ALUSI:90:10/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:90:10/r7.claim: Al-Imām relates this verse to the declaration that God guided the human being to the path, whether grateful or ungrateful.
ALUSI:90:10/r7.anchor: وقد جعل الإمام هذه الآية كقوله تعالى

ALUSI:90:10/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:10/r8.claim: Good is plainly a lofty path; evil descends from innate purity to wretchedness. Calling both paths elevated is explained either by predominance or by imagining ascent toward every goal.
ALUSI:90:10/r8.anchor: ووصف سبيل الخير بالرفعة والنجدية ظاهر بخلاف سبيل الشر فإن فيه هبوطاً من ذروة الفطرة إلى حضيض الشقاوة فهو على التغليب أو على توهم المتخيلة له صعوداً

ALUSI:90:10/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وابن المسيب
ALUSI:90:10/r9.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās, also related from Ibn al-Musayyib, interprets the two paths as a mother’s breasts.
ALUSI:90:10/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم من طرق عن ابن عباس أنهما الثديان وروى ذلك عن ابن المسيب

ALUSI:90:10/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:90:10/r10.claim: On this interpretation, the breasts are like two routes to a child’s life and nourishment, raised above the abdomen like a valley.
ALUSI:90:10/r10.anchor: لأنهما كالطريقين لحياة الولد ورزقه والارتفاع فيهما ظاهر والبطن تحتهما كالغور

ALUSI:90:10/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:10/r11.claim: The breast interpretation also draws on an Arab oath formula that swears by a mother and her two breasts.
ALUSI:90:10/r11.anchor: والعرب تقسم بثديي الأم فتقول أما ونجديها ما فعلت

ALUSI:90:10/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r12.speaker: علي
ALUSI:90:10/r12.claim: Reports cited in al-Durr al-Manthūr and Majmaʿ al-Bayān say ʿAlī rejected the breast interpretation and affirmed that the paths are good and evil.
ALUSI:90:10/r12.anchor: أنه كرم الله تعالى وجهه إن أناساً يقولون أن النجدين الثديان فقال لا هما الخير والشر

ALUSI:90:10/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:10/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:10/r13.claim: Al-Ālūsī suggests that those who chose the breast interpretation may have found it linguistically possible and especially apt as a blessing.
ALUSI:90:10/r13.anchor: ولعل القائل بذلك رأى أن للفظ يحتمله مع ظهور الامتنان عليه جداً

BAGHAWI:90:10/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:10/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI:90:10/r1.claim: Most commentators understand the two paths as good and evil, truth and falsehood, or guidance and error.
BAGHAWI:90:10/r1.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين : طريق الخير والشر ، والحق والباطل ، والهدى والضلالة

BAGHAWI:90:10/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:10/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب وابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب والضحاك
BAGHAWI:90:10/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, also held by Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib and al-Dahhak, takes the two paths as the two breasts.
BAGHAWI:90:10/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب عن ابن عباس : { وهديناه النجدين } قال : الثديين ، وهو قول سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك

BAGHAWI:90:10/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:10/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:90:10/r3.claim: Najd is a road on elevated ground.
BAGHAWI:90:10/r3.anchor: الثديين ، وهو قول سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك ، والنجد : طريق في ارتفاع

BAYDAWI:90:10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:90:10/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:90:10/r1.claim: The two high paths may be the paths of good and evil, or the two breasts.
BAYDAWI:90:10/r1.anchor: وهديناه النجدين طريقي الخير والشر أو الثديين

BAYDAWI:90:10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:90:10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:90:10/r2.claim: Najd originally means a raised place.

BIQAI:90:10/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:10/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:10/r1.claim: Biqāʿī contrasts ongoing present-tense blessings that preserve the faculties with past-tense guidance: intellect is first bestowed, then directed to good, and its hidden, stable character is thereby affirmed.
BIQAI:90:10/r1.anchor: ولما كان لله تعالى على كل أحد في كل لمحة منة جديدة في إبقاء هذه الآلات الثلاث ،   عبر فيها بالمضارع

BIQAI:90:10/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:10/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:10/r2.claim: God guides by the intellect to the two paths, good and evil; this makes a person hearing, seeing, knowing, and fit to bear religious responsibility.
BIQAI:90:10/r2.anchor: أي بما آتيناه من العقل { النجدين * } أي طريقي الخير والشر ،   وصار بما جعلناه له من ذلك سميعاً بصيراً عالماً فصار موضعاً للتكليف

BIQAI:90:10/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:10/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة
BIQAI:90:10/r3.claim: The Prophet says there are two paths, good and evil, and urges people not to prefer the evil path; what suffices is better than distracting abundance.
